# Contributing to MLP OS Archive

The archive welcomes My Little Pony-themed independent operating systems with
their own kernels, Linux distributions, and desktop themes or customizations.
Historical, discontinued, unfinished, and experimental projects are eligible.

- To suggest a project, open the [issue form chooser](https://github.com/Evan-Windproof/MLP-OS-Archive/issues/new/choose)
  and pick your language. A project name, category, short description, and at
  least one public source URL are sufficient to begin review.
- To add or improve a project record directly, follow the
  [project submission guide](../docs/PROJECT_SUBMISSION_GUIDE.md) and open a
  pull request against `main`.

Use the original language for source material and project titles. Translations
are welcome when available. Share material that can be discussed publicly and
credit the original creators.

An issue is a proposal. Maintainers review evidence, ask for missing information
when needed, and use a pull request to add an accepted record. A record
can be included with missing details. First-party evidence can establish
identity and documented history. See the
[inclusion policy](../docs/HISTORICAL_ARCHIVE_GUIDE.md#inclusion-and-assessment)
for separate verification, provenance, and testing criteria.

For release history, dated events, screenshot rights, and checksums, see the
[historical archive guide](../docs/HISTORICAL_ARCHIVE_GUIDE.md). Add unresolved
leads to the [research backlog](../docs/RESEARCH_BACKLOG.md) with source links.

## Ongoing maintenance

Use an issue for a new project, a correction, or additional historical
evidence. For an existing project, include its catalog URL, the specific
claim or field to change, and the relevant source. The localized project
forms can also be used for these updates.

- Check each new submission for scope, duplicates, and provenance. Apply
  the [inclusion policy](../docs/HISTORICAL_ARCHIVE_GUIDE.md#inclusion-and-assessment).
  First-party records can establish project identity and history.
- Update development status when the evidence supports a change. Keep it
  separate from identity verification, provenance, and testing status.
- If a download breaks, document when it was checked and distinguish an
  unavailable file from an unconfirmed one. Keep historical references and
  record verified archive or publisher links with their provenance.
- For screenshots and other media, record the original source, attribution,
  and known permission or license. Share a link while reuse rights are
  unclear. Do not upload private material to a public issue.
- For credit corrections or removal requests, identify the affected record
  or asset and explain what needs changing. Maintainers should review the
  source and rights, correct credit or remove the asset when warranted,
  and avoid repeating private details in the public record.

Use a pull request to preserve the evidence trail. Run `npm run check` and
`npm run build` before merge, and inspect the updated pages after deployment.
